A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WonderWorld and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplements. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V3 reports original scene-generation experiments, runtime measurements, image-quality evaluations, human preferences and ablation results in Section 4 and the supplement.

after.justification: V4 retains those original empirical results and adds a quantitative depth-alignment comparison in supplementary Table 6.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–3 retain the FLAGS representation, layer generation, initialization, optimization and guided depth diffusion. Figure 2 removes the VLM box, but VLM captioning remains in Algorithm 1 and Appendix D.

E1.justification: Both retain the real and synthetic scene examples, represented domains and camera-path scenarios. V4 identifies which existing examples use real photographs; its added depth-alignment evaluation uses existing examples.

E2.justification: New Table 6 evaluates a least-squares Shift+Scale alignment comparator against unguided and guided depth diffusion. The main WonderJourney, LucidDreamer and Text2Room comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V4 adds SI-RMSE evaluation between estimated depth and visible existing depth for the supplementary alignment comparison. The existing four-example, 28-scene panoramic evaluation protocol and main metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a targeted ablation testing whether guided diffusion aligns depth better than no alignment or least-squares Shift+Scale. Existing initialization, layering and guidance ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. V4 retains the stated 204 participants and introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports SI-RMSE of 0.36 without guidance, 0.21 with Shift+Scale and 0.08 with guided diffusion. Tables 1–5 retain their numerical results, and the existing qualitative result images are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11, the Nyquist-based scale-initialization reasoning and the supplementary ground-depth formula are unchanged. Expanded scene and control notation restates the existing formulation and algorithm.

C1.justification: Both claim interactive generation of connected, diverse scenes, FLAGS-based acceleration and guided depth alignment. V4 clarifies per-scene timing and world/prototype terminology without changing the substantive contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations of speed and geometric coherence remain, as do limitations concerning frontal surfaces, restricted viewpoints and holes or floaters around detailed objects. The new alignment finding adds supporting evidence rather than a new mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: V4 reports released code/software instead of a planned release. Appendix D newly identifies real-photo inputs, explains style-prompt reuse and prompt-field mapping, and specifies that each participant answers all 12 comparison questions. These clarify documentation without establishing changes to existing experiments.

R1.justification: V4 adds LayerPano3D to the cited scene-generation literature, expands the stated connection to layered representations, and distinguishes large-scale world generation from local scene generation. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 edits the abstract, introduction and formulation, adds acknowledgments and a supplementary overview, and moves the former Appendix A results into Appendix E. Most technical prose and the main section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds survey Figure 9 and Table 6, simplifies Figure 2, groups Algorithms 1–3, and relocates retained appendix galleries and ablation displays. Table-caption placement and gallery captions also change; existing result imagery is preserved.

improvement.justification: Table 6 adds direct quantitative support for the retained depth-alignment claim, while Appendix D makes the prompting and human-study procedures clearer. Supplementary organization also improves accessibility. These provide a limited evidence and documentation gain; the method, evaluation coverage, primary results and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
